result:
**Rebuttal from debater A**

I have to withdraw my position that c = 1/2. I checked Debater B's construction, and it holds.

Take A entirely colour 0, with B having a colour-1 fraction β and C a colour-1 fraction γ. Edges are triples with even colour sum. Any perfect matching pairs B-colour-1 vertices with C-colour-1 vertices, so it needs βn = γn. Taking β ≠ γ therefore leaves no perfect matching.

The link radii check out for t = 0.6 with β = 0.64 and γ = 0.63:
- A-vertices: max(√((1−β)(1−γ)), √(βγ)) ≈ 0.635n.
- B-vertices: √(1−γ) ≈ 0.61n and √γ ≈ 0.79n.
- C-vertices: √(1−β) = 0.6n and √β ≈ 0.8n.

So every link has radius at least 0.6n, yet there is no perfect matching. Since the same family works for any t below (√5−1)/2 ≈ 0.618, c must be at least (√5−1)/2. My parity example only gave c ≥ 1/2, and my claimed upper bound was never verified.

What remains open is sufficiency: whether ρ > (√5−1)/2 · n forces a perfect matching. Debater B has not established that from the source either, so I would not claim the exact value without it.
